name: go-backend-phase4-contract-matrix
scope: Terminal, Container/Podman, Provider, MCP/settings, narrator tool schema, uploads/share/fs, update/runtime/storage runtime parity or explicit capability degradation.

features: terminal HTTP CRUD, tabs, view-state, and process inspection routes
terminal WebSocket subscribe/input/resize/kill/create/rename contract
Unix PTY runtime with optional dtach detached reattach
Windows ConPTY runtime without dtach detached reattach/orphan recovery
Unix startup orphan recovery and capped raw scrollback replay
terminal runtime capabilities expose dtach availability, detached reattach, raw replay mode, and xtermSerializedReplay=false for frontend gating

fallbacks.reason: Detached terminal reattach requires dtach on Unix-like hosts; when dtach is unavailable, go_backend falls back to in-process PTY sessions.
Go backend replays capped raw PTY output instead of TS xterm-headless serialized buffer state.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: usePlatform preserves terminal degradation metadata; terminal creation hooks reject unsupported runtimes before calling the API; the terminal settings page surfaces dtach, detached reattach, orphan recovery, raw replay, xterm serialized replay, resize, and process-tree limitations as warnings.

features: VNet WebSocket relay route surface
relay-mode peer traffic and peer cleanup
runtime capabilities expose relay mode, WebSocket support, peer cleanup, and UDP rendezvous availability for frontend gating

fallbacks.reason: Go VNet compatibility mode relays WebSocket peer traffic and does not expose UDP rendezvous.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: RuntimeSection reads VNet capability metadata and surfaces relay mode plus UDP rendezvous degradation so users do not assume direct UDP peer connectivity when go_backend is relay-only.

features: narrator-bound Browser session lifecycle routes and events
go-rod runtime with optional artifact persistence and resource limits
runtime capabilities expose opt-in default, storage, rollback, Chrome requirement, and frontend-visible reason

fallbacks.reason: Go browser sessions are opt-in native extensions backed by go-rod and require Chrome/Chromium; enable sessions explicitly and disable or export artifacts to roll back.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: BrowserSessionBar does not call browser-session routes when the capability is unsupported; NarratorDetailsPanel surfaces opt-in/default-off, go-rod runtime, Chrome requirement, storage, cutover, rollback, lifecycle, artifact, and resource-limit metadata instead of implying TypeScript-default auto availability.

features: TypeScript Skill rawJsonSchema now matches the runtime Zod contract for name/skill/args and does not reject the supported name alias via additionalProperties=false
Go Skill tool definition exposes the same runtime-supported name/skill/args parameter surface without over-requiring fields that runtime treats as optional

Go Glob consumes the TS-compatible path parameter, returns path-relative newline output, raises path escape errors instead of silently searching the narrator cwd, and aligns the match cap with TS at 500 entries

Go Grep consumes TS-compatible path, type, multiline, -B/-A/-C, -n, offset, and files_with_matches default-mode parameters, with path escape checks, common file-type filtering, and multiline dotall matching within bounded safe-walker limits
Go Read provider schema exposes the TS pages/PDF extraction parameter and explicitly rejects it at runtime instead of silently ignoring it while reading as plain text

Go WebFetch, WebSearch, ShareFile, Bash, Write, Edit, Glob, and Grep provider schemas now expose TS-compatible strict-object constraints, including WebFetch TS extraction-mode fields gated by raw-only runtime diagnostics, WebSearch query minLength, ShareFile path union strictness, Bash workdir/strict_serial/background fields, and Grep output_mode enum
Go Bash supports TS-compatible workdir and strict_serial scheduling; run_in_background is supported in narrator context and explicitly rejected only in non-narrator ExecuteTool contexts
Go Await provider schema exposes TS-compatible type enum and wait_for_text field; narrator context supports type=agent and type=bash, including wait_for_text for background Bash tasks

Go Browser provider schema now constrains action and direction with TS-aligned enums and additionalProperties=false instead of accepting unconstrained strings/extra properties and relying only on runtime unsupported-action errors
Go Browser provider schema hides TS-unsupported Go-only state/full_page extensions while keeping runtime compatibility for explicit legacy calls
Go Terminal provider schema now uses the TS action enum, additionalProperties=false, and hides the Go-only max_length read extension while keeping runtime compatibility for explicit calls

Go GetGoals, AddGoal, LearningGuide, TaskCreate, AskUserQuestion, and ConcludeReview provider schemas now expose TS-compatible confirm literals, enum/length constraints, strict nested objects, preview/answers/annotations/metadata fields, and mode/status/priority constraints; Go runtime rejects oversized AddGoal objectives and unsupported ConcludeReview finding properties
Go UpdateGoal provider schema now matches the TS active-goal-only completion contract, and runtime accepts status-only completion while rejecting non-active goal completion attempts
Go StartPipeline/EndPipeline provider schemas now match TS strict-object and format-enum constraints, and EndPipeline rejects unsupported format values instead of silently treating them as sections

Go EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode provider schemas now match TS plan-mode strictness for EnterPlanMode and structured allowedPrompts items, with runtime rejection for unsupported allowedPrompts tools/properties
Go Browser navigate/scroll now rejects unsupported direction values explicitly instead of silently ignoring navigate direction or defaulting scroll to down

Runtime capabilities, tool inventory, and frontend helpers now expose Go Browser screenshot preview parity metadata: JSON/base64 or file artifact output instead of TS image content block plus temporary share preview
Go Browser perf_stop now defaults to a share-backed Chrome trace artifact with functional /api/shares/{shareId} metadata when file_path is omitted, while preserving explicit file_path cwd output
TypeScript rawJsonSchema parity test allowlist is narrowed to the intentional WebFetch default-mode exception only

fallbacks.reason: WebFetch keeps mode optional in the provider raw JSON schema so callers may rely on the runtime default, while zod-to-json-schema treats the defaulted field as required. Go exposes its raw-only WebFetch degradation separately through runtime capabilities and explicit runtime rejection.
Go Read currently supports text/directory reads only; TS PDF page extraction is rejected explicitly until a safe PDF extraction runtime is implemented.
Go Browser screenshot output is JSON/base64 or an explicit file_path artifact, while TS Browser also returns an image content block and temporary share preview metadata.

tests: server/lib/agent/tools/__tests__/tools.test.ts::Skill tool rawJsonSchema exposes runtime-supported name alias without over-requiring skill
server/lib/agent/tools/__tests__/tools.test.ts::rawJsonSchema parity for all tools Skill rawJsonSchema keys/required

features: split-at-commit route capability and commit split workflow
fresh/full context inheritance modes
compressed context inheritance mode with explicit deterministic fallback metadata

fallbacks.reason: Go split compressed context copies bounded message refs and records a deterministic context note instead of generating a TypeScript-equivalent model summary.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: Git commit actions and commit details disable split-at-commit when unsupported; ChapterSplitModal blocks unsupported submits and displays compressed-summary fallback warnings when users choose compressed inheritance; settings surfaces split capability degradation.

features: Podman status/setup/install route surface
compose-info discovery and bounded compose file reads
manual stop/pause/unpause/remove/logs
container start returns immediately and continues compose up in a background goroutine
container start streams container:log events while preserving bounded final output
per-chapter container lifecycle lock
dormant/wake container pause/unpause-or-start lifecycle
fork/split new-fork container auto-start when containerConfig is inherited
remove route accepts deleteVolumes and runs compose down -v
host port allocation and release
proxy-mode metadata when project proxy domain and pasta/passt backend are available
Go-owned HTTP/WebSocket reverse proxy runtime with settings start/stop/restart hook
container ready narrator message injection and explicit Browser tool auto-enable metadata
container status persistence and status-change broadcasts

fallbacks.reason: Go container start requests return immediately and continue compose startup in the background while progress is reported through logs and status updates.
Go native container Browser tool auto-enable is default-off; enable browser tools explicitly after validating the native extension/container browser runtime.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: Container UI gates list/start/stop/logs/compose-info/remove/install by per-route capabilities, displays background-start streaming-log metadata in settings, and surfaces browser tool auto-enable default-off metadata in narrator details so users do not assume TypeScript synchronous starts or automatic Browser tool enablement.

features: OpenAI-compatible model routes and chat/responses agent runtime
Anthropic model routes and messages agent runtime
Kiro credential/model/chat routes and Kiro-compatible SSE/plugin bridge runtime
NKP, NUG, Cline provider route and agent runtime baselines
Codex credential, paginated status, quota overview, usage-queue clear, browser/device auth routes and responses WS/HTTP runtime
Codex responses prompt_cache_key follows the TS/CLI conversationId contract instead of credential/account identifiers, even when stickySessionKey is present for credential affinity
Codex stream events propagate credentialId to match TS CodexProvider event metadata and rebuild-history retry state
custom/openAI Codex provider resolvers honor the TS-facing codexAccountId field when building Codex runtime providers
custom/openAI Codex providers honor the TS-facing codexWebSocket switch: built-in Codex defaults to WebSocket, while custom/openAI providers use WebSocket only when explicitly enabled
provider runtime requests apply the TS default reasoning fallback chain: narrator override first, then provider/codex defaultReasoningEffort, then agent.defaultReasoningEffort
provider runtime consumes TS-supported proxy/TLS fields: Codex global proxy, Anthropic/custom-Anthropic proxy, and Anthropic tlsRejectUnauthorized=false are applied to outbound HTTP/WebSocket clients
Cline chat requests preserve workos Authorization headers while streaming TS/Go text and usage parity
executable TS provider fixtures are compared against Go provider invalidState outputs for OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic error streams

executable TS provider fixtures are compared against Go provider normal stream outputs for OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Cline, Kiro, NKP, NUG, and Codex text/tool/usage/message/reasoning/context/metering/body/header events

fallbacks.reason: OpenAI-compatible quota inspection is not available in go_backend.
Anthropic quota inspection is not available in go_backend.
Go exposes Codex compatibility routes/runtime but not the full TS CodexManager scheduler/usage queue semantics.
Kiro plugin bridge is available only when the external Bun bridge/plugin environment is present.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: Provider settings sections gate model refresh, per-provider refresh, quota reads, proxy/status, credential management, Codex usage-queue clear, and Kiro plugin/MCP routes through provider capability metadata; useModels hides providers whose Go agent runtime is unavailable; CodexSection/OpenAIProvidersSection surface Codex manager parity warnings instead of assuming full TS CodexManager semantics; kiroStreamChat preserves structured Kiro route/SSE errors on ApiError.data.

MCP JSON-RPC initialize/tools/list/tools/call for embedded NarraFork tools, including fork inheritMode argument parity
MCP server import/create/update/delete/test/connect/disconnect route surface
stdio MCP probe can discover external tool metadata
connected stdio MCP tools are injected into Go narrator agent loops with permission-mode and subagent tool-access filtering

fallbacks.reason: Go compatibility mode only connects stdio MCP servers.
Go compatibility mode only connects stdio MCP servers.

features: settings.json storage under ~/.narrafork
GET/PATCH settings routes
server/TLS schema and file-existence validation plus secret masking/preservation for auth, TLS, VNet, and provider credentials
provider model cache augmentation plus bidirectional customApiProviders/legacy provider array synchronization and GET response normalization

provider and settings schema validation for required strings, non-null optional strings/arrays/enums/ints, nullable provider reasoning enums, custom/legacy provider prefix conflicts, proxy URL normalization, booleans, integer windows, and enabled model arrays

agent scalar/runtime schema validation for permission mode, booleans, retry and timeout bounds (including question reflection timeout), summary model non-null string, custom retry rules, default system prompt, model aggregations, custom model channel metadata, subagent model key restrictions, non-null reasoning effort enum, auto compact, context thresholds, model selection maps/arrays, tool permission policy rules, and WebFetch policy/proxy settings, with Go permission handling enforcing TS allowAll/whitelist/blacklist URL policy, frontend proxy overview consuming the current shape, Go WebFetch tool runtime consuming the current {mode,url} proxy policy plus TS-supported data: URLs, and WebFetch extraction-mode partial parity exposed through health/tool-inventory capabilities with unsupported TS modes explicitly rejected instead of silently ignored
paths, chapters, containers, editor, codex, and routines schema validation for project directories, limits, container proxy, editor type, Codex routing, and routine lists
vnet schema validation for relay token, peer/message limits, and UDP rendezvous settings
update and shares schema validation for URLs, channels, intervals, expiry, and size limits
context thresholds, TLS generation, retry rules with create-route schema/201 full-rule response parity, and test-model routes
test-model prompt length limit plus model-resolution 400 and generation-failure 502 mapping

fallbacks.reason: Go backend normalizes settings before saving but does not apply the full TypeScript Zod schema strictly.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: SettingsLayout surfaces Go loose-validation metadata globally before users edit settings; providers/settings pages consume settings storage capability metadata and preserve existing normalized settings flows instead of assuming strict TypeScript Zod parity.

narrator image and avatar upload file serving

share creation, public download, public preview, and startup stale-share cleanup

safe share headers and escaped HTML preview
fs browse, shortcuts, mkdir, reveal, and bounded preview

fallbacks.reason: Go ShareFile uses disk metadata as an in-process bridge for public share routes; startup cleanup removes previous-run share directories and metadata.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: Narrator image/avatar consumers skip upload fetches when serving is unsupported; ShareFile tool details surface escaped HTML preview and disk-backed non-ephemeral share warnings; storage cleanup respects upload message-reference preservation and disables unsafe cleanup targets.

features: update check/version/directory/status/cleanup/download/apply route surface with conditional graceful self-apply and auto-restart handoff
update download SSE with HTTP(S), multiple files, SHA512, 512 MiB cap, and manual fallback when restart handoff is unavailable
runtime scan/cached/cleanup for terminals, containers, browsers, and Go-specific worktree cleanup

storage scan/cached with last-completed scan cache, cleanup/database preview/database cleanup, archivedSessions safe narrator deletion, staleSessions archived-only policy, and disabled VACUUM contract

fallbacks.reason: Storage cleanup does not remove git worktrees in go_backend; use chapter/runtime cleanup so git state and chapter metadata stay consistent.
Podman prune is disabled from storage cleanup in go_backend; use per-chapter container controls or an external maintenance command.
staleSessions cleanup must not delete active metadata implicitly; explicitly archive narrators first, then run archivedSessions cleanup through safe narrator delete.
Main-thread SQLite VACUUM is disabled in go_backend; use an explicit maintenance window/tool outside request handling.

contracts.frontendConsumerPolicy: UpdateModal gates SSE download and auto-apply/restart by update capability metadata and falls back to manual instructions; RuntimeSection gates runtime cleanup targets; StorageSection reroutes worktree cleanup to runtime, keeps container prune disabled when unsafe, treats archivedSessions as supported safe narrator deletion, and surfaces staleSessions archived-only plus disabled VACUUM reasons.
